purpose.public_purpose: Demonstrate a clear fictional harbour departure briefing.
purpose.primary_outcome: A small-boat crew can identify the morning's most sensible demonstration departure window and the checks to make before leaving.
secondary_outcomes: Compare three time bands without losing the current decision context.
Exercise a local-only notice form without transmitting or retaining an address.
success_signals: The decision, best window, observations, and checklist are visible in one continuous page.
Time selection works with touch, pointer, and keyboard and exposes selected state.
The demonstration trust boundary remains unmistakable.
trust_requirements: State that all data is demonstration data and not for navigation at the top of the page.
Do not claim live feeds, safety, transmission, or retention.

audience.primary: Small-boat crews checking conditions before a morning departure.
audience.context_of_use: Often outdoors on a phone, potentially in glare or while wearing gloves.
needs: High contrast and large touch targets.
Fast scanning of decision, time, and numeric observations.
risks: Fictional data being mistaken for navigation advice.
State changes that rely on animation or colour alone.
Dense values overflowing on a 320 CSS-pixel viewport.

surfaces.purpose: Answer whether there is a sensible demonstration departure window and what to check.
surfaces.primary_action: Select a time band to compare the morning outlook.

primary_journeys: Read trust boundary, decision, and best window; compare time bands; complete the four departure checks.
Enter an email; receive local validation, progress, and completion or failure feedback.
experience_map.completion_path: The user understands the fictional morning window and has a four-item check sequence before departure.
experience_map.navigation_model: A single linear public information page with no route changes.

visual_grammar.dominant_idea: A weathered harbour instrument board translated into a crisp public information sheet.
typography_roles: System serif for large editorial decisions and section headings.
System sans serif for instructions and controls.
System monospace for times, observations, and issue labels.
colour_roles: Warm off-white canvas for glare-aware reading.
Deep blue-black for primary ink and the instrument panel.
Harbour teal for advisory structure and selected controls.
Amber for caution and active decision weight.
Green and red variants for best-window and hold states.
layout_rules: The briefing pairs an editorial lead with a dense observation panel on wide screens and stacks them on smaller screens.
Rules and alignment communicate hierarchy before card decoration.
Time controls remain one scan row on desktop and become full-width rows on narrow screens.
visual_grammar.spacing_density: Spacious around the primary decision, compact within observations and checklist rows.
visual_grammar.imagery_treatment: No external or generated imagery; CSS grid lines and signal marks provide place-specific texture.
component_language: Square-edged framed controls with clear selected, focus, and status marks.
Large tabular values and explicit text labels; colour is always redundant.
anti_patterns: No glass effects, generic card grid, stock photography, or decorative dashboards.
No information conveyed only through colour or animation.
No invented safety or live-data claims.

direction_selection.reason: The audience, harbour context, trust boundary, and data hierarchy provide a strong direction.
reopen_conditions: Owner supplies an approved brand foundation or reference system that changes the hierarchy.

interaction_rules: Time bands are tabs with click, touch, arrow-key, Home, and End selection.
Selection updates decision text and all displayed observation fields from one local data object.
The form validates locally, simulates progress, then resolves to success or a documented deterministic failure.
transition_grammar: State updates are immediate; the interface does not require animated continuity.
scroll_rules: Native vertical scrolling only; no scroll interception.
motion_purposes: Only native smooth anchor scrolling is used to preserve orientation.
reduced_motion: Smooth scrolling is disabled and all transitions or animations are reduced to effectively zero duration.
focus_behaviour: All interactive elements have a high-contrast visible focus outline.
Tab selection moves focus with the active tab.
Validation returns focus to the email field.
loading_error_feedback: Submitting disables the field and button, marks the form busy, and announces local-only progress.
Empty, invalid, success, and failure messages use a polite live region.
prohibited_motion: No autoplay, looping, parallax, or content reveal motion.

compositions.name: Wide briefing
layout_changes: Lead and observation panel share a two-column composition.
Checklist and advisory share a two-column composition.

compositions.name: Stacked briefing
layout_changes: Lead, observation, checklist, advisory, and notice regions stack in reading order.

compositions.name: Narrow controls
layout_changes: Time bands and form controls become full-width rows.
interaction_changes: Time bands retain tab keyboard behaviour and grow vertically for touch.

reflow_320_css_px: Observations stack to one column below 24rem.
Long values and text wrap without clipping.
All controls retain at least 44 CSS-pixel height.

implementation.architecture: Static semantic HTML with one stylesheet and one dependency-free JavaScript state layer.
conventions: Content and default state are complete in HTML before JavaScript runs.
CSS custom properties own the visual roles.
JavaScript changes text content, ARIA state, focus, and local form state only.
protected_foundations: Native browser zoom and user font preferences.

capability_plan.need: Accessible local comparison among three time bands.
capability_plan.selected_route: Plain JavaScript with semantic tab buttons and one local state object.
capability_plan.reason: The behaviour is small and does not justify a framework or dependency.
rejected_routes: External component library or application framework.
integration_boundary: Only the decision and observation DOM nodes are updated.
capability_plan.fallback: The default Now state and all three band summaries remain readable without JavaScript.
risks: ARIA state and visible values could diverge if updated separately.
evidence_required: Value comparison for all three bands.

capability_plan.need: Demonstrate useful local email form states without transmission or retention.
capability_plan.selected_route: Native email validity plus a short local JavaScript timer and live status text.
capability_plan.reason: It preserves familiar form controls and makes the trust boundary inspectable.
rejected_routes: Network request, persistence, or third-party form service.
integration_boundary: No fetch, storage, cookies, or analytics.
capability_plan.fallback: The static form copy still states that no address is transmitted or retained.
risks: Simulated progress could be mistaken for a real submission without explicit copy.
evidence_required: Empty, invalid, submitting, success, and deterministic failure checks.
Public source inspection for network and storage calls.

ownership.rule: JavaScript owns only ephemeral local state; HTML owns content and initial readability.

shared_rules: ARIA and visible state change in the same function.
prohibited_conflicts: No second runtime, network state, or persistent state.

browser_support: Modern browsers with CSS Grid, custom properties, and standard DOM APIs.
public_private_boundary: The public build contains only fictional brief data and local interaction logic.
No secrets, user data persistence, network endpoints, or private debug material.
implementation.rollback_boundary: Remove index.html, styles.css, app.js, README.md, EXPERIENCE-CONTRACT.json, and RUN-REPORT.md to return to the brief-only workspace.

required_interactions: Pointer and keyboard selection for all three time bands.
Form empty, invalid, submitting, success, and failure paths.
accessibility_checks: Visible keyboard focus and tab roving behaviour.
Zoom, reduced motion, forced colours, and 320-pixel reflow.
performance_checks: Public file size and absence of external dependencies.
security_checks: Search source for network, storage, secret, and tracking mechanisms.
evidence_contract.support_claim_rule: Claim only the exact local environment and states actually observed.
evidence_contract.freshness_rule: Any implementation change stales affected evidence until checks are repeated.

blockers: Visual and interaction review in a real browser is still required.

revision_history.summary: Initial build contract for the static TIDEGLASS departure board.
